=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:1814-1820 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The trusted-author check for the hand-over marker in rb_judge_red_check_scan (`if author in ("github-actions[bot]", "app/github-actions") or (login and author == login):`) leaves out the GraphQL login `github-actions`, which is how gh_pr_with_all_comments returns the judge's own hand-over author.
  WHY: In the default unsigned setup, the judge treats its own hand-over as untrusted, so the pre-judge dedupe does not fire. A re-run on the same red head calls the LLM again, posts a second `ai:final-ci-handover:v1` comment, edits the labels again and sends another ERROR alert, which breaks the "handed to a person once" and "no repeat judge runs" requirements. Severity is MAJOR from all reviewers that stated one.
- prompts/mode-judge-review-blocked.txt:33,155-161,258 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The DEFAULT-tier prompt is 258 lines, over the 250-line limit in tests/prompt_size_budget.py.
  WHY: The required `quick / static-checks` check already fails with "258 lines exceeds DEFAULT limit of 250", so the PR cannot merge. All reviewers that stated a severity rated it BLOCKER.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:1823-1829,1897-1902 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: rb_judge_red_check_scan counts `ai:final-ci-repair-request:v1` markers from any comment author (openai_gpt-6-luna adds that repair-cap markers are also counted from any author). The gate accepts these markers only from the pipeline login or `github-actions[bot]` of type Bot.
  WHY: Anyone who can comment on the PR can post a forged marker that forces `reason=head_requested` (or `head_cap`). The judge then skips the automatic repair for that head and posts a hand-over, adds `ai:needs-human` and sends an ERROR alert. Severity disagreement: NIT from anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, MAJOR from openai_gpt-6-luna, unstated by z-ai_glm-5_3-flash; the highest is used.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:1897-1925 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The repair-request comment is posted before the dispatch. If every dispatch candidate fails (`dispatch_failed`), the status stays checks_failed but the request marker stays on the PR, and the next judge run on that head takes `head_requested` and hands over without retrying the dispatch.
  WHY: One transient `gh workflow run` failure turns the automatic repair into a permanent human hand-over before any repair has run. Severity disagreement: NIT from anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, MAJOR from minimax_minimax-m3 and openai_gpt-6-luna; the highest is used.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:1657-1712 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The embedded Python SECTION parser in render_review_rb_ci_failures_file keeps matching `failed[N].<field>:` headers inside a `log_tail` block. Untrusted CI log text can therefore override `details_url`/`name`/`summary`, add fake job entries or cut the log tail short.
  WHY: An injected `details_url` controls which run ID the later `gh api .../actions/runs/<id>/jobs` call reads, and corrupted fields reach the judge prompt and `judge_ci_failure_summary`. Severity disagreement: MAJOR from minimax_minimax-m3, NIT from openai_gpt-6-luna, unstated by z-ai_glm-5_3-flash; the highest is used.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:1960,2129-2139 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `RB_JUDGE_RED_CHECK_REPAIR_ENABLED` gates only the routing. render_review_rb_ci_failures_file, its up to 3 `GET actions/runs/<id>/jobs` calls and the `=== CI FAILURES ON THE JUDGED HEAD ===` prompt section all run regardless of the switch.
  WHY: With the switch set to false, the judge prompt and API usage still change, so pre-#10063 behaviour is not restored. Severity is MAJOR where stated.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:3688,3851-3858 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: When a required check is red, the `merge_with_followup` branch refuses with `judge_skip_reason=blocking_check_runs` (line 3857) and never calls `rb_judge_route_red_checks`, which is called only at lines 3186 and 3303.
  WHY: The prompt prefers `merge_with_followup` at IS_FINAL, so a red head gets no repair-request marker, no dispatch, no hand-over and no `ai:needs-human`, and stall recovery keeps re-firing the judge on the unchanged head. Severity is MAJOR where stated.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:rb_judge_route_red_checks (`elif [ "${request:-0}" != "0" ]; then reason="head_requested"` branch) | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: Nothing ties the request marker to the review run it dispatched, so a judge run that starts on the same head while that run is queued or running sees request=1 and hands over at once.
  WHY: The PR gets `ai:needs-human`, an ERROR alert and a hand-over comment saying the repair "cannot run again" while the repair is still in progress (rated NIT).
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:1570,1617 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The new env var `RB_JUDGE_CI_FAILURES_MAX_RUNS` (default 3, clamped 0-3) has no README row.
  WHY: Operators cannot find the variable, and §20/§30 require a README row with a default for every new variable (rated NIT).
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:3182-3184,4085 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The new statuses (`final_ci_repair_requested`, `final_ci_handover`, `final_ci_handover_posted`) and `judge_skip_reason=final_ci_handover_posted` are not declared in any central enum or contract.
  WHY: Downstream helpers that pattern-match on the old status set may silently treat these statuses as unknown (rated NIT).
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:1925-1930,1960-1961 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: rb_judge_route_red_checks sources `review_freshness_ci_failed.sh` and dispatches a workflow run as a side effect of `merge` on a red head, so the implicit-execution surface is broader than the declared switch scope.
  WHY: The switch gates routing but not the renderer, so a trust-boundary mismatch remains (rated NIT).
- scripts/review_autofix_step_evaluate_gate.sh:1958-1964 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: The gate now accepts a judge request marker in place of the `ai-review/head-gate` success status, and it accepts that marker from any `github-actions[bot]` comment, not only from the review-blocked judge.
  WHY: A `github-actions[bot]` comment whose last line is the marker could select the repair commit path on a head the pipeline never approved. The reviewer calls this hardening, not a demonstrated exploit (rated NIT).
- PR Description:"Closes https://github.com/shubhodeep1/coding-workflows/issues/10063" | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The PR body uses the auto-close keyword "Closes" with #10063, which this reviewer calls a tracking issue.
  WHY: The reviewer argues that merging would auto-close the orchestrator's tracking issue, which §21/§19 forbid (rated BLOCKER). anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 explicitly rejected this finding because #10063 is a pipeline sub-issue ("Refs #9669, #9394"), not the tracking issue.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "With a required check red on the head, the judge's `merge` is not accepted as the outcome. The run instead takes the final-CI repair path for that head, even when MAX_AUTOFIX_ITERATIONS and MAX_REVIEW_BLOCKED_RETRIES are used up."
  expected_change_site: scripts/review_rb_judge.sh, `merge_with_followup)` branch (blocking_check_runs handling, lines 3851-3858)
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: rb_judge_route_red_checks is called only at lines 3186 (merge) and 3303 (terminal fix), the merge_with_followup branch writes judge_skip_reason=blocking_check_runs (line 3857) without routing, no diff hunk touches the merge_with_followup branch, and the prompt prefers merge_with_followup at IS_FINAL (the PR #9679 "Retry: 2 of 2" situation)
- requirement: "One switch, default on, restores today's behaviour when off."
  expected_change_site: scripts/review_rb_judge.sh, render_review_rb_ci_failures_file call (line 1960) and the `=== CI FAILURES ON THE JUDGED HEAD ===` prompt block (lines 2129-2139)
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: RB_JUDGE_RED_CHECK_REPAIR_ENABLED is checked only in the pre-judge guard and rb_judge_route_red_checks (lines 1585, 1876, 1952, 3186, 3303), rendering and prompt emission run unconditionally with up to 3 jobs API reads, and no test in tests/test_review_rb_judge_red_check_repair.py checks that the section and prompt are absent with the switch off
- requirement: "When the repair's caps are also used up, the PR is handed to a person once ... No repeat judge runs on an unchanged head after that hand-over (the dedupe of #9991 applies)."
  expected_change_site: scripts/review_rb_judge.sh, rb_judge_red_check_scan trusted-author set (line 1819) / rb_judge_final_ci_handover_posted / pre_judge skip (lines 1953-1962)
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: Line 1819 recognises only "github-actions[bot]" and "app/github-actions", and the judge's own hand-over reads back through GraphQL with author "github-actions", so the once-only guarantee and repeat-run suppression fail in the default unsigned setup
- requirement: "§20, §30: ... README rows for any new variable (each with a default)."
  expected_change_site: README.md variables table (around line 181)
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:1617 reads RB_JUDGE_CI_FAILURES_MAX_RUNS (default 3, clamped 0-3) via `RB_CI_MAX_RUNS="${RB_JUDGE_CI_FAILURES_MAX_RUNS:-3}"`, and README.md has no row for it; only RB_JUDGE_RED_CHECK_REPAIR_ENABLED was added
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:rb_judge_red_check_scan, the embedded Python `if request_re.search(body): request += 1` (around line 1823, no author check), which feeds `elif [ "${request:-0}" != "0" ]; then reason="head_requested"` in rb_judge_route_red_checks (around line 1897) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The judge counts `ai:final-ci-repair-request:v1` markers from any comment author, while the gate accepts them only from the GH_PAT login or `github-actions[bot]` of type Bot.
  WHY: Untrusted comment text turns off the repair for that head (reason=head_requested) and triggers the hand-over comment, the `ai:needs-human` label and an ERROR alert. Suggested fix: count `request` only from trusted authors.
